s01: The sky is blue. The sunset is red. Same sun, same air.
s03: Air scatters short wavelengths hard, and long ones barely at all.
s04: So blue light gets knocked sideways. Red mostly carries on straight.
s05: At noon, you are not looking at the sun. You are looking at air.
s06: The blue you see was knocked out of somebody else's sunbeam.
s07: At sunset, the light comes in low, through hundreds of miles of air.
s08: By the time it reaches you, the blue has been knocked out of it.
s09: What arrives is what nobody scattered.
s10: So a red sunset is not the sun changing colour.
s11: It is the leftovers of a blue sky happening somewhere else.
